# ChartBook

> Data pipelines with provenance. ChartBook connects a team's data pipelines, in any language, so each one builds on another's exact, versioned output: every chart traces back to its sources, every input is verified by hash, and everything lands in one catalog that people browse and agents build on.

A **pipeline** is a folder in git with a manifest, `chartbook.toml`, that declares what it makes (dataframes, charts, models, files, notebooks, notes). A **snapshot** is everything one pipeline built at one commit, by hash, kept in a **store**; another pipeline **pins** it in `chartbook.lock` and reads it by name. A **catalog** is one site over every snapshot in its stores. Every page is also published as Markdown: `guide/agents.html` is `guide/agents.md`.

## The five commands

Five commands cover most of what people do. The middle three are typed in a pipeline's folder, and `chartbook run` runs the script that `chartbook.toml` names as `build` under `[scripts]`. `chartbook --help` lists them first:

| You type | It does |
|---|---|
| `chartbook init` | Once: starts a project from the template, in a new folder |
| `chartbook run` | Builds this pipeline: pins what it reads, runs its build script, looks for everything `chartbook.toml` declares, and makes its snapshot when everything is committed |
| `chartbook pin --update` | Takes the newest snapshot of each pipeline it reads |
| `chartbook catalog open` | Opens the catalog in your browser: every snapshot in your stores |
| `chartbook install agents` | Once per project: teaches your coding agent ChartBook |

## Get started

- [Quickstart](docs_src/getting-started.md): `pip install chartbook`; a pipeline from three files (manifest, script, README); `chartbook docs build`; what `index.json` records
- [Explore a Catalog](docs_src/tutorials/explore-a-catalog.md): clone and build three pipelines (`chartbook run --snapshot` in each; the third pins the other two, so `chartbook pin --update` first), `chartbook catalog build` / `open`, follow a model to its source through a pin, ask an agent, `chartbook add tutorial/treasury_curve`
- [Let Your Agent Use the Catalog](docs_src/guide/agents.md): what is there (`chartbook ls --json`), what it is (`chartbook get-docs ID`), use it (`chartbook add`, `data.load`, `chartbook path`), can it be trusted (`chartbook lineage`)
- [Start a Project From the Template](docs_src/guide/starting-a-project.md): `chartbook init`; each data source chosen brings a dataframe and a chart
- [Vocabulary](docs_src/guide/vocabulary.md): the words, defined once. A manifest asks, a lockfile records what was got, a snapshot records what was made, an index records what a site shows; repository → index → pages → site; a writer per site tool
- [CLI Reference](docs_src/reference/cli.md): `chartbook init`, `chartbook docs build`, `chartbook docs open`, `chartbook run`, `chartbook snapshot`, `chartbook restore`, `chartbook lineage`, `chartbook pin`, `chartbook pin --update`, `chartbook run --check`, `chartbook trust`, `chartbook path`, `chartbook publish`, `chartbook catalog`, `chartbook ls`, `chartbook get-docs`, `chartbook data`, `chartbook store`, `chartbook config`, `chartbook install claude-skill`

## Guides

- [Documenting a Pipeline](docs_src/guide/documenting-a-pipeline.md): Describe charts, dataframes, notebooks, notes, models and files in `chartbook.toml`; `[files]` for files that are not tables (archives, text, PDFs, images, arrays)
- [Depending on Another Pipeline](docs_src/guide/depending-on-pipelines.md): snapshots, pins and the lockfile; `chartbook run --snapshot` (them), `chartbook pin` / `pin --update` (you); never read another pipeline's folder; `--frozen` in CI; model versions and labels
- [Keeping Costly Outputs](docs_src/guide/keeping-costly-outputs.md): `keep = true` on an output that cost money or compute (a paid API run's output, a trained model): every version stays in the store, `chartbook restore` puts it back, `chartbook run` stops before remaking it (`--remake`); the doit recipe
- [Reading and Writing Data](docs_src/guide/reading-and-writing-data.md): write your outputs by name (`data.path("x")` makes the folder; a folder dataset is written with `partition_by`); read any pipeline's data with `data.load()` / `data.sql()`; another pipeline's folder or glob has files and no path (`NoSinglePathError`): `data.files()`, `assets.gathered()` for a loader that takes a directory; `data.scratch()` and `[project] scratch` for throwaway files
- [Catalogs and Stores](docs_src/guide/catalogs-and-data.md): Aggregate pipelines; load any cataloged dataset with `data.load()`; every snapshot of every pipeline is its own site under `versions/`, listed on the catalog's Versions page; a `[pipelines]` entry with no path shows a pipeline from the store alone; `chartbook store ls` says which snapshots are standalone or shared; remove snapshots with `chartbook store gc`, never by hand
- [Reading From a Databricks Warehouse](docs_src/guide/reading-a-warehouse.md) (experimental): `[sources.x] backend = "databricks"` after `pip install chartbook[databricks]`; `DATABRICKS_HOST` + `DATABRICKS_TOKEN`; a token goes only to the host the machine names; lazy reads; a Databricks Free Edition walk-through
- [Plotting](docs_src/guide/plotting.md): One call produces interactive HTML plus static PNG/PDF
- [Writing a Plotting Backend](docs_src/guide/plotting-backends.md): The `PlottingBackend` contract, the `chartbook_plotting` entry-point group, and a complete example
- [How the Build Works](docs_src/guide/how-the-build-works.md): resolve (the index) → write (a writer: pages from the index and the files it names; Sphinx by default, MkDocs with `[project] writer = "mkdocs"` and `pip install chartbook[mkdocs]`) → build (the site tool); incremental builds (Sphinx); template overrides in the project root

- [Roadmap](docs_src/roadmap.md): what works now (one machine, a store in a shared or synced folder), what is experimental (Databricks), what is next (Delta pins, Snowflake, other warehouses, a database as the store, an MCP server)

## Reference

- [Configuration](docs_src/reference/configuration.md): Complete `chartbook.toml` reference with all fields, types, and defaults
- [Python API](docs_src/reference/api.md): `from chartbook import data; lf = data.load(pipeline="my_pipeline", dataframe="df_id")` — pipeline accepts a bare name or a scoped name (`myorg/my_pipeline`)

## Key Commands

```bash
chartbook init            # Scaffold a new pipeline project
chartbook init --github   # ...then git init, commit, create a private GitHub repo with gh, and push
chartbook docs build      # Render the HTML documentation website
chartbook run             # THE command: pin what has no pin, run [scripts] build, fail if a declared output was not written, and make a snapshot when everything is committed
chartbook docs build -f   # Force overwrite existing docs
chartbook docs build -f --watch  # Rebuild incrementally on every file change
chartbook docs open          # Open the generated site
chartbook run --check              # CI gate: missing metadata, broken paths, dependencies that cannot be found, expiring licenses
# every build also writes docs/index.json: a record per pipeline, dataframe, column, chart,
# notebook, note, model and files asset, each with an ID (scope/pipeline:kind/name) and a content hash,
# and docs/llms.txt: a line per pipeline, dataframe, chart, model and files asset with its ID and page link
# (a catalog's also links each version's own llms.txt); read it first to find your way around a site
chartbook path <name>        # Print the path chartbook.toml declares for a dataframe
chartbook path chart/<name>  # ...for a chart (also notebook/<name>, note/<name>, model/<name>, file/<name>)
chartbook path file/<name> --files  # the asset's files, one per line, sorted: a folder's files, a glob's matches
chartbook path <pipeline>:<name>  # another pipeline's asset: the pinned copy in the store (a first read pins it)
chartbook path model/<name>@<version>  # a version of a model: by the start of its hash, or by a label from [models.<name>.aliases]
chartbook path <dep>:model/<name>@champion  # another pipeline's labelled version, as pinned in chartbook.lock (pin reads labels from the snapshot; pin --update moves them)
chartbook index diff BEFORE AFTER [--json] [--exit-code]  # what changed between two builds, from their index.json: data, pins, versions, labels, staleness
# A model is out of date when what it was trained on has moved: its page says so, index.json has stale_inputs, `chartbook run --check` warns; `chartbook run` retrains
# In Python: data.sql("select * from {df_a} join {df_b} using (date)") runs SQL with dataframes named in braces (DuckDB, or the warehouse of a databricks source);
# data.ref("df") is a dataframe's name in SQL; data.connect("source") the raw connection. [sources] in chartbook.toml.
chartbook publish            # Stage publishable files to a directory
chartbook create-data-glimpses  # Create data summary report
chartbook run --snapshot     # The strict form of `chartbook run`, for a script that must end with a snapshot: refuses before building with anything uncommitted, exits 1 where no snapshot can be made
chartbook snapshot           # Seldom needed (`chartbook run` ends with one): a build already on disk into the store, labelled with the commit; refuses unless its pins account for every dependency
chartbook restore [name...]  # The mirror of snapshot: this pipeline's assets back on disk from its snapshots; with no names, every `keep = true` asset that is missing; never over a file
chartbook lineage            # Every snapshot upstream, walked through the pins and checked by hash; --check exits 1 on a gap, --rehash re-hashes the bytes, --json; `chartbook snapshot --deep` refuses on an upstream gap
chartbook add acme/rates     # Declare a dependency by its ID ("acme/rates" = {}) and pin its newest snapshot from the store, no folder or clone; --as NAME, --commit C; a bare name (rates) writes the one stored ID ending in it, else nothing
chartbook pin                # Freeze what [dependencies] have: each one's newest snapshot, into chartbook.lock
chartbook pin --check        # Write nothing; exit 1 unless the lockfile is complete and every pin is met: its file is in the store, or a build of your own of the pinned commit holds the same rows up to the pin's last date (no shared store: `git checkout <commit>` in the upstream, `chartbook run --snapshot`) (CI, read-only shared store: a folder, or s3://bucket/prefix with chartbook[s3])
chartbook pin --update [dep...]    # Move pins forward to each dependency's newest snapshot; says of each dataframe whether it gained rows or its earlier rows changed
chartbook run [script]       # Run a [scripts] entry here (default: build). For build: pin what has no pin, run it, exit 1 if it did not write something chartbook.toml declares with a path (or the file of a DuckDB source), then make a snapshot when everything in the folder is committed, chartbook.lock too (else exit 0 and a last line `not snapshotted: N files are not committed`: commit, run again). At a terminal, a build that reads a pipeline [dependencies] does not declare is offered `chartbook add` of it, and built again. Where pipelines it reads are not in the store, it builds nothing and lists them in the order to build, each with the commands to paste (`chartbook pin` prints the same list). Never builds in a folder it depends on, but --upstream builds and snapshots one with no snapshot
chartbook run --frozen       # Pin nothing, fetch nothing, write nothing but the store's note for gc; build only if every pin is in the store
chartbook run --remake       # Build even though a `keep = true` asset is missing while the store has it; without it, run and build stop and say `chartbook restore`
chartbook trust              # Say this folder's pipeline is yours to build (at a terminal the first build asks: y trusts, r renders without its code, Enter stops); until then a build of it runs as a build of files from a store (--render, --repository, --list, --forget)
chartbook store ls [ID]      # Every snapshot, standalone (its folder holds every file of its version) or shared (only what changed; the rest sit in other snapshots' folders), with what its folder holds; remove snapshots with gc, never by hand
chartbook store info         # Which store this machine uses, what set it, and the cache folder
chartbook store verify       # Re-hash everything in the store; exit 1 if an object changed
chartbook store gc           # Remove old snapshots and what nothing names (asks first; --keep-days, default 7; --keep-lineage keeps every snapshot upstream of a kept one; --aggressive lets tags, branches and labels keep nothing; every version of a `keep = true` asset stays)
chartbook store migrate      # Move a store made by ChartBook 0.2 to 0.3's layout (a folder per pipeline, a folder per snapshot, each file once); once, after every machine has 0.3; --dry-run first
chartbook store export ID --to DIR   # One pipeline's snapshots into DIR/pipelines/<pipeline>/, to send (--latest, --snapshot COMMIT[@MADE_AT])
chartbook store import DIR    # Copy the snapshots in DIR (an export, or a pipeline's folder) into this store, each file checked against its record
chartbook config             # Configure default catalog path
chartbook install agents     # The Claude Code skill for the user, and a ChartBook section in the project's AGENTS.md (between two marker lines; run again after an upgrade)
chartbook install claude-skill  # The Claude Code skill, user-level (--project: ./.claude/skills/chartbook); its SKILL.md names the ChartBook it is for
chartbook catalog init       # Make the machine's catalog, ~/.chartbook/catalog.toml, ahead of time (the first command that needs it makes it over your store, asking at a terminal)
chartbook store add NAME URL  # Add a store; a pipeline enters by snapshot
chartbook catalog disable <id>  # Leave a pipeline out of the catalog's builds; `chartbook catalog enable <id>` brings it back
chartbook catalog build   # Render the catalog site
chartbook catalog open       # Open the catalog site in the browser. At a terminal it asks to build first when the site is behind the stores (snapshots made or cleared since its last build), or was never built; off a terminal it opens what there is and says how far behind it is
chartbook ls                 # List all pipelines, dataframes, charts
chartbook ls dataframes      # List dataframes only
chartbook data get-path --pipeline <id> --dataframe <id>   # Get parquet path
chartbook data get-docs --pipeline <id> --dataframe <id>   # Print docs content
chartbook ls --json                       # Every pipeline and asset of every kind, as JSON
chartbook get-docs <pipeline>:chart/<name>  # Any asset's write-up, by its id; a bare <pipeline> is its README
```

## Python API

```python
from chartbook import data

lf = data.load(pipeline="acme/markets", dataframe="market_data")       # through the catalog: its newest snapshot; Polars LazyFrame
df = data.load(pipeline="markets", dataframe="market_data", format="pandas")  # a bare name when only one matches
rates = data.load("fed_yield_curve:treasury_rates")                    # inside a pipeline: a dependency's pinned copy, by reference
path = data.path("my_dataframe")                                        # inside a pipeline: where its own chartbook.toml puts it

from chartbook import assets
paths = assets.files("file/filings")             # a [files] asset's files, sorted (works for a dataframe of many parts too)
table = assets.index("dep:file/filings")         # LazyFrame: path, size_bytes, sha256, a column per key=value folder; a dependency's from the store's record
docs = data.get_docs(pipeline="markets", dataframe="market_data")       # the write-up, as text
docs = assets.get_docs("markets", "chart/volume")                       # any asset's write-up; assets.get_docs("markets") is the README
```

## Minimal Configuration Example

All `[project]` keys are optional (an empty `chartbook.toml` is a valid pipeline manifest). Project type is inferred: a `[pipelines]` registry table means catalog, otherwise pipeline. Each chart and dataframe needs exactly one of `docs_path` (external markdown file) or `docs` (inline markdown).

```toml
[project]
name = "My Pipeline"
description = "Analytics pipeline description"
maintainer = "Your Name"

[charts.my_chart]
name = "My Chart"
description = "Chart description"
dataframe = "my_data"
path = "./_output/chart.html"
docs_path = "./docs_src/charts/chart.md"

[dataframes.my_data]
name = "My Data"
description = "Data description"
sources = ["Source"]
path = "./_data/data.parquet"
date_col = "date"
docs = "Documentation for this dataset."
```

## Directory Structure

```
my-pipeline/
├── chartbook.toml      # Configuration
├── README.md           # Required; becomes the site front page
├── _data/              # Parquet data files
├── _output/            # Generated HTML charts
├── docs_src/           # Markdown documentation
│   ├── charts/
│   ├── dataframes/
│   └── site/           # Optional custom site pages
└── src/                # Python source code
```

## Catalogs and stores in 0.4.0

A catalog is `catalog.toml`, listing stores rather than working folders. `chartbook catalog migrate` keeps a backup when upgrading the old file. `chartbook catalog build` renders hubs over stored versions. `chartbook docs build` renders a pipeline site. A task runner owns the documentation step of `chartbook run`.

```console
chartbook store add NAME URL
chartbook store remove NAME
chartbook store move ID --to NAME --dry-run
chartbook ls stores
chartbook ls versions
chartbook link ID FOLDER
```

Writes follow catalog routing; reads search every store. Dependency entries may name a portable publishing URL, with anonymous S3 reads via `?anonymous=true`. Links explicitly override pins during local development, are recorded in build provenance, are ignored in CI and frozen runs, and prevent snapshots until removed.
